subject: Bridge Week leadership: QBR playbook + targeted OKR checks
messages:
From: jonas.weber@redwood.com
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Bridge Week leadership: QBR playbook + targeted OKR checks

Team —

Quick bridge-week note ahead of the Friday QBR: I drafted a compact "QBR playbook" (attached) to keep the exec session tight and unblocked. TL;DR: three narrative lanes (Customer Health & Renewals, Serving Reliability + Capacity, Cost/Unit Economics) with one explicit decision per lane.

Wins (short):
- Renewal motion with Acme Analytics is on track; CSM reports exec sponsor lined up for July 7.
- Hosted API latency improved after the kernel update deployed last week (p95 down ~12%).

Risks / watch:
- Dedicated onboarding for the Enterprise X pool slipped: commit->provision window now shows a 6 business-day delay (tracking in capacity_commitments.csv). Impact: predicted throughput shortfall for mid-July spikes if we don't re-route.
- Canary inference job flagged a small BLEU/regression on the reranking model for long tail prompts (SERV-154). We need a short mitigation plan before we push that variant more broadly.

Asks (owners + deadlines):
1) Laura: please confirm the two executive talking points (renewal headline + SLAs) you'd like us to surface in the QBR deck by EOD Thu.
2) Karthik: can your infra team confirm temporary routing policy (regional fallback to eu-west) and sign off on a 48-hour burst from Dedicated pool by 10:00 PDT Thu? See capacity_commitments.csv attached.
3) Marcus: can you validate whether the BLEU drop is quantization-related or data-shift? Short triage note by 2pm Thu would be ideal.
4) Vanessa: consolidate one slide of ask/actionable decisions from Product (we'll keep it to 2 bullets) — due Thu 5pm.

Attachments: QBR_playbook_v1.pdf, OKR_snapshot_Week26.xlsx, capacity_commitments.csv

I kept the playbook intentionally short so the deck stays <12 slides; the drive link has the slide stub and suggested speaking order.

Thanks —
Jonas
Jonas Weber
VP, Operations
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Bridge Week leadership: QBR playbook + targeted OKR checks

Jonas —

Thanks for the crisp playbook. A couple quick notes from Exec comms:
- For the Renewal lane, lead with the commitment risk mitigation (how we’ll ensure the Acme renewal closes even if onboarding slips). That shows ownership.
- For the SLA headline, call out p95 improvement and the concrete plan to cover the Dedicated shortfall (routing + 48-hour burst).

I can take the two talking points; will send a one-pager to you and the deck owner by Thu noon. Also: do we have a single slide that lists the asks (decision + owner + date)? If not, I’ll add one.

Laura Bennett

Jonas / all —

Acknowledged. Quick infra update:
- We ran a provisioning simulation overnight; the Dedicated pool delay is coming from node allocation contention in us-west (cloud partner queued nodes). Short-term mitigations: 1) enable eu-west fallback on the routing layer (low risk for latency-sensitive customers flagged as tolerant), 2) allow a controlled 48-hour burst from our reserved spare capacity. Both are doable but require ops approval (I’ll raise the change set).
- I’ve attached capacity_commitments.csv with the new simulated routing numbers and the estimated cost delta for the 48-hour burst.

Regarding the SERV-154 regression: infra traced the canary to the quantized runtime path on some gpus; Marcus, that aligns with your note last sprint about the quant kernel mismatch. I’ve added a link to the ticket in related_links. If Marcus can confirm whether a parameter-tolerant rollback is acceptable, we can keep the old runtime on canary and avoid a broad rollback.

Action items:
- Karthik: submit the routing change and burst approval request by Thu 10:00 PDT. (Owner: karthik.iyer)
- Marcus: triage SERV-154 and propose either a patched kernel or a temporary runtime pin by Thu 14:00 PDT. (Owner: marcus.lin)
- Vanessa: we’ll need one slide listing this mitigation plus cost delta — Thu 17:00.

Thanks —
Karthik Iyer
Head of Infra

All —

I dug into the regression and confirm it's correlated with the newer int8 kernels on a narrow subset of long-sequence reranking prompts. Initial findings:
- Repro locally when using runtime-v2-int8 on the Llama-rerank variant; not present on float16 runtime.
- Likely causes: a combination of tokenization edge cases + reduced dynamic range in the quant path.

Short-term proposal (for Thursday):
1) Pin the canary to float16 runtime (no rollback of model weights) — low blast radius and quick to flip.
2) Add a targeted test in CI that exercises the long-sequence reranking prompts (I’ll push a test by Thu 10:30).

If infra enables the routing fallback and the 48-hour burst, we should be safe for the QBR window. I’ll prepare a one-paragraph note explaining the mitigation for the deck (Marcus action item).

Marcus Lin
Director, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
